summary: Quarterly renewal/expansion check-in. Lynx is nearing contract renewal and wants to add capacity (2x reserved GPU pools), enable an additional EU region, and discuss a short contract extension to align procurement. Security questions (SOC2, KMS) were raised; Redwood to provide docs. Next steps: pricing, benchmark, security pack, draft amendment.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-05
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Park (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Rina Gomez (Redwood CSM), Maya Li (Lynx Head of MLOps), Jon Rivera (Lynx CTO), Priya Nair (Lynx Infrastructure)

[00:00] Alex Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. Quick sanity check, audio okay?
[00:08] Maya Li: Yep loud and clear, thanks Alex.
[00:12] Samir Patel: Cool. So goal for today is to walk through the capacity/region ask and nail down next steps for the renewal amendment.
[00:20] Jon Rivera: Sounds good. We're pretty close on the renewal but want to make sure performance scales when we double traffic for summer campaigns.

Summary / context-ish:
[00:35] Rina Gomez: For context, current committed capacity is a single reserved GPU pool (8 A100-ish equiv), monthly commit. Lynx usage has been spiking, and procurement wants a 6-month extension + a 2x capacity bump to avoid throttling. They also want EU region availability for GDPR workloads.

[01:10] Maya Li: Yeah our main ask: 2x reserved capacity, add Frankfurt region for EU-sensitive flows, and keep hosted API for dev/test but route production through Dedicated for lower 99th perc latency. Also need clarity on KMS integration and audit logs.

[01:38] Alex Park: Got it. We can absolutely do the capacity bump and add region, couple of things to align on — expected QPS and percent of traffic you want routed to Dedicated vs hosted fallback, and whether you want cross-region failover or single active region.

[02:05] Maya Li: We expect peak QPS of ~350 requests per minute for the chat endpoint, with bursts up to 600 for short windows. Latency target is P95 < 220ms for short prompts; for long context prompts maybe a bit higher.

[02:30] Samir Patel: Right. For those numbers, recommended is 2x reserved pools (we'll size with GPU type) with autoscale burst capability. On latency SLOs, we'll want to run a benchmark on your prompt set — the KV cache and continuous batching behavior matter a lot.

[02:50] Priya Nair: Quick question — does Dedicated support custom KMS/HSM for key wrapping in the private region? We need to ensure encryption-at-rest keys are customer-managed.

[03:05] Alex Park: Yes, Dedicated supports customer-managed keys via KMS integration; on private deployments we also offer HSM options. I'll share the security pack, but short answer is yes — you can bring your KMS and we can integrate with the key rotation policies.

[03:25] Jon Rivera: And audit logs? We need per-request traceability for compliance.

[03:31] Samir Patel: We provide detailed audit logs at the tenant and route level, and token-level cost/latency breakdowns in the console. There can be small sampling gaps in streamed responses, but full request/response hashes are stored depending on retention. We'll include the exact retention options in the security doc.

[03:55] Maya Li: One thing procurement flagged: we might need a short amendment for 6 months rather than a full one-year to line up with budget cycles. Is that possible?

[04:05] Alex Park: Yes, we can do a 6-month amendment for the reserved capacity, then revisit full-term during renewal. I'll draft language and share.

[04:18] Speaker 1: (mumble) pricing details — how does billing work when we add a region?
[04:23] Alex Park: Good question. Billing for reserved capacity is per pool; adding a region adds a separate reserved pool pricing line if you want dedicated capacity in EU. For egress and cross-region traffic we'll show estimated costs in the sheet. We'll send a sample invoice line items.

[04:45] Samir Patel: Also worth mentioning smart routing — you can route EU traffic to FR and non-EU to US, with automatic fallback to a regional compatible model if capacity constrained. That helps keep latency low.

[05:10] Priya Nair: How does KV cache behave across regions? If we have active-active, do we replicate cache? Concerned about consistency.

[05:20] Samir Patel: We typically keep KV cache per region to avoid cross-region latency; active-active will have per-region caches which may lead to cold starts if a user's requests jump regions. For most production flows we recommend active-passive with fast failover if tight context continuity is needed.

[05:45] Maya Li: That makes sense. For our use case, we need session stickiness to the region for at least 30 minutes. Is that supported?

[05:55] Alex Park: Yes, session affinity can be configured at the routing policy level; we'll include suggested configs in the benchmark plan.

Technical clarifications / small transcription glitches here and there:
[06:10] Jon Rivera: On the model side, we're using a mix of open models for embeddings and a smaller fine-tuned chat model for inference. Any concerns about quantization or perf when moving to Dedicated?

[06:25] Samir Patel: Some models when quantized behave differently; our platform supports quantization profiles and will recommend a profile based on the model architecture and sequence length. We'll validate that in the benchmark. Sometimes names get munged in logs, e g 'Red wood Dedicated' in some transcriptions but that's just the export.

Benchmark & testing planning:
[06:50] Samir Patel: Proposal: 2-hour benchmark window where we run your top 50 prompts at production concurrency and measure P95/P99, and token costs. We will also test failover to EU region. Need your infra folks to open a peering window and allow test IPs.

[07:10] Priya Nair: We can schedule that. We'll need exact IP ranges and test plan.

[07:20] Samir Patel: I'll send the plan; we'll include warmup scripts to populate KV cache so results match production more closely.

Discussions around procurement and renewal:
[07:40] Maya Li: Procurement asked for an SLA that covers latency and availability, and a credit structure for missed SLOs. Can we get that in the amendment?

[07:50] Alex Park: We have SLA addenda for Dedicated customers; standard availability and latency credits can be included. We'll add the specifics to the draft amendment.

Pricing talk (a little fuzzy audio / overlapping):
[08:12] Speaker 2: So roughly what's the delta to double capacity?
[08:16] Alex Park: High level, committed reserved capacity scales linearly, but we can offer a stepped discount for short-term 6-month bump. I'll include two pricing options in the sheet — 6-month amendment price and 12-month commit price.

[08:38] Jon Rivera: And EU region adds about 20% to the monthly spend?

[08:42] Alex Park: Ballpark yes, depends on GPU type and expected usage; we'll put conservative estimates in the sheet.

Security / compliance deep-dive (light):
[09:00] Maya Li: A few specifics — does Redwood retain raw prompts or can we disable content retention? We need to limit storage for some PII flows.

[09:10] Samir Patel: You can configure redaction and retention policies; for PII-sensitive flows we recommend disabling retention and using encrypted logs with short retention TTLs. We'll include config examples.

[09:30] Priya Nair: KMS integration — we use GCP KMS, can you support that?

[09:36] Alex Park: Yes, we support GCP KMS, AWS KMS, and HSM options for private. Integration notes forthcoming. There might be a slightly higher ops lead time for HSM.

[10:00] Maya Li: Anything else on the legal side? Procurement asked about subprocessors and DSAR handling.

[10:08] Rina Gomez: We'll include our subprocessor list and DSAR SLA in the pack. If you need specific amendments we can coordinate with legal.

Recap and explicit next steps:
[10:30] Alex Park: To recap — Lynx wants 2x reserved capacity and an EU (Frankfurt) region, and a 6-month amendment aligned to procurement. Action items: Alex sends pricing and draft amendment; Samir sends benchmark plan; Priya confirms peering and test window; Rina shares usage and renewal dates.

[10:55] Jon Rivera: That sounds right. Let's target the benchmark week of 5/18 and aim to have contract language by 5/12 so procurement can review.

[11:10] Maya Li: One last note — if benchmarks show higher latency we may request a temporary burst buffer. Is that doable?

[11:18] Samir Patel: Yes, we can enable burst capacity for a short period; we'll include cost/time estimates.

Closing, small cross-talk and pleasantries:
[11:35] Alex Park: Great — thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and scheduling invites.
[11:40] Maya Li: Thanks all.
[11:42] Jon Rivera: Appreciate it.

End of transcript (approx 42 minutes). Note: occasional transcription errors present (speaker labels and product names sometimes malformed).
